question: What is the unit of measurement for frequenсу?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hertz (Hz)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hertz (Hz)** is the **SI unit of frequency**, which measures the number of cycles of a periodic wave per second.
 
• It is named after the German physicist **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**, who made significant contributions to the understanding of electromagnetic waves.
 
• 1 Hertz represents **one cycle per second**. For example, a frequency of 50 Hz means there are 50 cycles of the wave occurring each second.
 
• The unit is widely used in various fields such as **physics, telecommunications, acoustics, and electronics** to describe the frequency of waves, including sound waves, electromagnetic waves, and alternating current.
 
• Applications of frequency measurement in **Hertz** include **radio broadcasting** (e.g., FM radio operates at 88-108 MHz), **electricity** (standard power supply frequency is 50 Hz or 60 Hz), and **digital systems** (e.g., processor clock speeds in GHz).
 
• The **Hertz** is a derived unit, and its dimensional formula is **T⁻¹**, where T represents time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Millisecond**__

 __
 
• A **millisecond** (ms) is a unit of time and is equal to **one-thousandth of a second** (1 ms = 0.001 seconds).
 
• It is commonly used in fields like **computer science** and **electronics** to measure short time intervals, such as **response times**.
 
 
 
• **Pascal**__
 __
 
• The **Pascal (Pa)** is the SI unit of **pressure**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as **one newton per square meter** (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).
 
• This unit is used to measure pressure in various fields such as **fluid dynamics, meteorology, and material science**.
 
 
 
• **Joule**__
 
 
• The **Joule (J)** is the SI unit of **energy**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as the **work done** when a force of one newton moves an object one meter (1 J = 1 N·m).
 
• It is used in fields like **physics, engineering, and thermodynamics** to measure energy, work, or heat.
